answer.rationale: Memory 57 is strongest because it directly reports qualified revenue and no measurable retention harm, though longer-term durability is not established. Memory 44 directly supports qualified pipeline through enterprise sales-assisted flows, but does not report realized revenue or retention. Memories 31, 73, and 86 provide useful leading indicators—activation, acquisition/revenue lift, onboarding completion, and time-to-value—but omit qualified-revenue quality, margins, and long-term retention; memory 73 additionally risks discount-driven, unsustainable revenue. Memory 91 is least supported because it reports only short-term engagement and first meaningful action, with no evidence of revenue, qualification, retention, or durability.
